newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-Generale Bank open to links.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Generale Bank open to links.

text.p: Generale Bank, Belgium's biggest bank, on Tuesday said it would remain independent for now but was not against an alliance with a partner, notably fellow Belgian bank Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL).

"We have a stand-alone policy for now but we are receptive to the message that a bigger Belgian bank would be a good thing," chief executive officer Ferdinand Chaffart said in reply to questions at a news conference about the bank's 1996 earnings.

Asked about comments from Generale Bank shareholder Ste Generale de Belgique (SGB), which has said it was interested in a merger between Generale Bank and BBL, Chaffart said: "The ideal partner does not exist. One has to look at what the opportunities are. But this could be a beautiful opportunity."
Asked whether a merger with BBL might lead to a marked cut in jobs and branches, Chaffart said: "I think it would be possible to do this in a controlled manner, without much pain."

Chaffart's apparent interest in an alliance contrasts sharply with the independent stance he took last year around the same time, when Generale Bank and BBL shareholders also indicated that they favoured a merger.
Chaffart, however, said he had not changed his mind.

Generale Bank shares rose five percent on Monday and two percent on Tuesday to close at 14,025 francs, after SGB chief executive Philippe Liotier was quoted as saying that "We are interested in a merger between Generale Bank and BBL but not at any cost."
Liotier's comments, which dated from the end of January, appeared in an investment club magazine interview.

Liotier said that a Generale Bank-BBL merger was blocked by Dutch Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING), which controls 20 percent of BBL stock and wants to keep a 20 percent stake in a new merged entity. He said this was unacceptable.
A Generale Bank source told Reuters on Tuesday that ING could not block a merger with its 20 percent stake as a 25 percent stake was needed for a blocking minority.
The source said ING would have a stake of about eight percent in a new merged entity, which would give it a right to representation on its board, adding: "That is unacceptable for us."
Last week BBL chief executive officer Michel Tilmant also said he had a "stand alone" perspective on his bank's future but would not be against an alliance. ING has so far has refused all comment.
Generale Bank's 1996 group net profit rose 10.4 percent to 15.10 billion francs ($430 million) from 13.67 billion in 1995.
Total assets rose to 5,544 billion francs from 4,739 billion, partly due to the first-time consolidation of Dutch unit Generale Bank Nederland and French asset management unit Fimagest.
The bank proposes to pay a 395 francs net dividend per share, up 10 francs.
All bank shares were well bid on the Brussels bourse on Tuesday as merger fever boosted the entire market.
Kredietbank ended 1.71 percent higher at 13,350 francs, BBL gained 1.1 percent at 8,290 francs, while Credit Communal closed 2.67 percent higher at 4,040 francs. ($ = 35.16 Belgian Francs)
